Consulting services for associations

Ricochet serves professional and trade associations with five services: member research, membership modeling, branded campaigns, technology and AI roadmaps, and fractional staffing. We help you find the right combination.

Member Research

How do I understand what my members need and how satisfied they are?

Ask them the right way, then act on what they say. Ricochet designs and runs association member research and turns every finding into a recommendation. Most projects start with a member survey analyzed segment by segment, with confidence intervals so leaders know which differences are real. We add focus groups or AI-assisted interviews when the question needs members' own words. Explore Member Research

Membership Modeling

How do I grow dues revenue and membership counts?

Find the association member types and dues rates that grow your revenue and membership roster. Ricochet benchmarks your performance against industry averages, then models and forecasts scenarios in an interactive financial model. The work ends in a transformation roadmap your team can carry out. Explore Membership Modeling

Brand and Campaign Studio

How do I keep my association relevant, with a clear story and campaigns that drive response?

Set the story your association tells, then build the system that produces campaigns at speed. We clarify the value proposition and codify it in an AI-ready design system. That system lets us use AI to produce campaign assets in every format, with a person reviewing each one before launch. Explore Brand and Campaign Studio

Tech and AI Roadmaps

How do I evolve my technology to serve members better?

Map every system your association runs, from the AMS to email, events, learning and the website, and decide what to do with each one over the next five years: keep, replace, build or connect. Ricochet scores each move on its value against its effort and five-year cost, with the budget built in, so you fund a plan instead of a wish list. We connect and clean member data first and time big changes, such as an AMS switch, to contract renewals. AI comes in short steps once the data is ready. Explore Tech and AI Roadmaps

Fractional Staffing and Training

How do I add senior talent to my team and stay within budget?

Add senior or systems expertise for part of each week, with no wait for recruiting and no full-time role to carry. Unlike offshore teams or freelancers, our fractional staff know associations and hold HubSpot, Mailchimp, AMS and AI certifications. They set strategy and do the hands-on work, and your staff come out more skilled. Training sits alongside it, from Association Academy courses to custom workshops. Explore Fractional Staffing and Training

How do I understand what my members need?

Stop guessing. Field a member survey your board can trust, then act on what it tells you. Ricochet runs association member surveys from the first question to the final recommendation.

How it works

What happens in a member survey project?

Four phases, each one feeding the next, from the research objectives to the last recommendation.

  1. Administration

    A kickoff workshop sets the research objectives, the segments and the roles. Weekly status meetings keep it on track.

  2. Discovery

    We review your past research and talk with staff and stakeholders, so the survey asks what you actually need to know.

  3. Fieldwork

    We write, design and program the survey, then send the invitations and reminders that drive response.

  4. Recommendations

    We analyze every response and deliver findings, each with a recommendation your team can act on.

Why Ricochet

What makes a Ricochet member survey different?

Numbers your board can trust, cut the way your board thinks, with a next step attached to each one.

  • Segments, then slices

    Every top-line number is cut by the segments your board worries about. Double and triple slices are standard, not an add-on, so one survey yields dozens of findings instead of one average.

  • Statistical confidence on everything

    We report the confidence interval alongside every score. A 4 and a 3 are the same number until the interval says otherwise, so you never react to noise in a small subgroup.

  • Every comment, coded

    AI makes open-ended answers analyzable at scale. Every comment is coded into themes, so hundreds of write-ins become a finding instead of a few quotes.

  • Findings ship with action

    Every finding comes with a recommendation, sorted into easy wins your team can move on now and long-term initiatives that need budget or buy-in.

What you get

What do I get at the end of a member survey?

A formal findings report your leaders can act on, with a recommendation for every finding.

  • A survey built for your membersThe survey instrument, written and designed for you.
  • Fielding handled for youProgramming, invitations and reminders, managed by Ricochet.
  • Every response analyzedEach result cut by segment and reported with its margin of error.
  • Recommendations you can act onA findings and recommendations report, plus the full dataset.

Survey findings often lead to the next step. Findings on dues feed Membership Modeling, and findings on perception feed the Brand and Campaign Studio.

Questions

What associations ask about member surveys

Do we need a survey or focus groups?

A survey validates: it tells you, with statistical confidence, how many members hold a view. Focus groups explore: open discussion that shapes ideas before you decide. Most associations start with a survey.

What does a member survey cover?

Questions are ordered by what each one is worth: a loyalty score benchmarked against the industry, member benefits ranked by segment, questions on your current strategic initiatives, communication preferences, and demographics.

Can you survey lapsed members and prospects?

Yes. Nonmember surveys reach lapsed members and prospects, so you learn why people leave and what would bring them in.

What do we get at the end?

A formal report with a recommendation for every finding, split into easy wins and long-term initiatives, plus the full dataset for your permanent records.

How many responses do we need?

Enough for each segment you want to compare. We report confidence intervals, so you know which differences are real and which are noise.

What do members actually value?

Ask them, then cut the answer by segment. A member survey has members rate and rank each benefit, then compares the results across member types, career stages and regions. A benefit that ranks low overall can matter most to one segment. Ricochet reports each result with its margin of error, so you act on real differences, not noise.

How do we get a real response rate on a member survey?

Keep it short enough to finish. Put the highest-value questions first, and pre-fill what your AMS already knows, such as member type and years of membership. Then send a planned series of invitations and reminders. Ricochet writes, programs and fields the survey, and drives response through those reminders.

How do we learn how members prefer to be contacted?

Ask about channel and frequency in your member survey. A communication preferences block asks which channels members want, such as email, LinkedIn, text or print, and how often they want to hear from you. The results guide your content calendar and where you invest, and they can feed a preferences center where members choose for themselves.

    Types and tiers

    Types charge different rates for the same benefits. Tiers charge different rates for different benefits.

Questions

What associations ask about membership modeling

Do we need member research first?

No. Modeling starts with an audit of your current model and data. Member survey findings make the model sharper when you have them.

What is the difference between member types and tiers?

Member types charge different rates for substantially the same benefits. In individual membership associations, types usually follow career stage, such as student, early career and retired. In trade associations, they usually follow a member company's annual revenue. Tiers charge different rates for substantially different benefits.

What is a firm or group membership model?

One organization pays for a group of its people to join, instead of each person joining alone. We model how a group rate affects members, revenue and renewals.

How do associations grow membership?

By pulling three levers together: the benefits members value, dues rates set against peers, and member types or tiers that fit each audience. Recruitment offers, such as intro rates for students and young professionals, help too. Ricochet models each option in a working financial model, so you see the effect on members and revenue before you commit.

What causes member retention to drop?

First-year members are usually the weak spot. In the 2026 MGI Membership Marketing Benchmarking Report, first-year retention averages 61% at individual associations, against 79% overall. Weak onboarding, dues out of line with perceived value and benefits that miss key segments all add to it. A membership model shows which lever moves your renewal rate most.

How often should an association raise dues?

Many associations raise dues a little every year, tied to an inflation measure such as the Consumer Price Index. Larger increases have no set schedule. The right time is when the model shows an increase will grow revenue without losing more members than you can afford.

How do associations raise dues without losing members?

Model the increase before you decide. About half of associations raised dues in 2025: 49% of individual and 53% of trade associations, according to the 2026 MGI Membership Marketing Benchmarking Report. Ricochet models renewal and recruitment at each rate, so you see how many members a rate could cost and how much revenue it adds.

How do you forecast the impact of a dues change?

In an interactive scenario dashboard. Leaders adjust renewal rates, recruitment pace and dues, and see members, revenue and payback change.

What associations ask about technology and AI

What should an association do about AI first?

Start with your data. AI is only as good as the member records it reads, so a roadmap begins with a data audit and the first agents clean and connect data before they touch members.

Can AI work with our AMS?

How do you keep member data safe with AI?

Data protection is part of every roadmap. Each agent gets access only to the data it needs, and your team stays in control of it.

What is an AI agent?

Software that carries out a routine task on its own, such as sorting an inbox or flagging duplicate records, and reports back to staff. Agents live in your own platforms, so your team owns them.

How long does a technology roadmap take?

About 90 days from discovery to a roadmap and budget, with optional help building integrations and agents after that.

When should we replace our AMS?

When it holds you back and its contract is coming up. Time the switch to the renewal date and notice window, so you don't pay for two systems at once. Make one big change a year, so staff can absorb it, and connect and clean your member data first. A roadmap sets the timing and the five-year cost.

How do we keep member data in sync across our systems?

A roadmap maps every system and data flow first. Ricochet then builds the integrations, including the AMS Connector for HubSpot or Mailchimp.

Why do members have duplicate records and login problems?

Usually because records are created in more than one place, such as event registration, the website and the AMS, without a shared ID.
